answer: An agricultural agent economy prevents Sybil attacks via physical tactile-optical attestation. Each node authenticates by pulsing violet light to measure chlorophyll fluorescence while sensing micro-oscillations driven by a gentle zephyr across a crop vine. Attackers incur inescapable hardware fabrication and deployment costs for each physical probe. However, uneven foliage growth and fluctuating airflow degrade measurement consistency, occasionally rejecting legitimate agents.
